matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: Before moving any stick, compute the numeric values of both sides (including any addition or subtraction) and determine the numeric imbalance. Then consider a single‑stick move that can correct that imbalance.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the equation is false and you need to decide which stick to move.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick without first checking the numeric difference, leading to a change that doesn't fix the imbalance.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and a V appears on the side that must increase, move one of its diagonal sticks to form an X, increasing the value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to increase a side by 5 and a V is present on that side.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from V but not forming a proper X, leaving an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral that contains at least one I to another numeral that can accept an additional I without violating Roman‑numeral rules.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance matches the ±1 change caused by moving an I and both source and target numerals stay valid after the move.
matchstick.example: Removing an I from a solitary I (leaving it empty) or adding an I to a numeral that would become invalid (e.g., turning V into VI incorrectly).

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign (single horizontal) and an equals sign (two horizontals) are present, you can move one horizontal stick from the equals sign to the minus sign, turning the equals into a minus and the minus into an equals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance can be fixed by swapping the operators, typically after evaluating the imbalance and seeing that the swap yields equality.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from '=' and leaving a stray line that is not a recognized operator, or failing to create a proper '-' or '=' after the move.

matchstick.title: Ensure a valid '=' remains when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: When taking a horizontal stick away from the equality sign, verify that the remaining single horizontal still forms a valid '-' sign, and that the added stick creates a valid operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you remove a stick from '=', to avoid leaving an invalid operator.
matchstick.example: Taking a horizontal from '=' and ending up with a single line that is not a valid '-' sign.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and an X appears on the side that must decrease, move one of its diagonal sticks away, turning the X into a V and reducing the value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to decrease a side by 5 and an X is present on that side.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X but not forming a proper V, leaving an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Evaluate expressions when computing numeric imbalance
matchstick.principle: Fully evaluate any arithmetic expressions (e.g., addition, subtraction) on each side before comparing numeric values, to correctly assess the imbalance.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after parsing the equation, before considering any stick moves.
matchstick.example: Treating 'II - IX' as concatenation rather than subtraction, miscalculating the numeric imbalance.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick across equality
matchstick.principle: When the numeric imbalance is exactly 2, move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral on the side with excess to a numeral on the other side, adjusting both sides by 1 each.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When imbalance is 2 and a suitable I is available on the larger side.
matchstick.example: Moving an I across the equality sign but leaving the source numeral invalid (e.g., removing the only I).

matchstick.title: Reposition I before X to change XI to IX
matchstick.principle: If a numeral 'XI' appears, moving its I‑stick to the left of the X changes it to 'IX', decreasing its value by 2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to reduce a value by 2 and the numeral XI is present.
matchstick.example: Moving the I from XI but placing it elsewhere, resulting in an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Convert '+' to '-' by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: If a '+' operator is present and a V numeral appears on the side that must increase by 1, you can move the vertical stick from '+' to the V, turning '+' into '-' and V into X, increasing that side by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to increase a side by 1 and both a '+' and a V are present on that side.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' but not converting V to X, leaving '+' as an invalid shape.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any numeral can donate a stick, ignoring the composition rules of Roman numerals.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that the source numeral will remain a valid Roman numeral after the stick is removed.

matchstick.description: Providing an invalid equation after moving a stick (including incomplete or unreachable solutions)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on moving a stick but doesn't verify that the resulting symbols form a syntactically valid equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After moving a stick, verify that each numeral and operator is a recognized Roman numeral or allowed operator.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid '=' sign in the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may remove a horizontal from '=', forgetting that a single horizontal is a minus sign, not an equals sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When taking a stick from '=', ensure the remaining sign is a valid '-' and that the added stick creates a valid operator.

matchstick.description: Not verifying numeric equality after transformation; resulting equation may be syntactically valid but numerically false
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may stop after achieving a syntactically correct equation without checking the arithmetic.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Compute the numeric values of both sides after the transformation and confirm they match.

matchstick.description: Moving more than one stick (or removing multiple sticks) violates the single‑stick rule
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may try to adjust multiple symbols simultaneously.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure exactly one stick is relocated; count the sticks removed and added.
